items.title: [phys.org] Full-scale wave test shows salt marshes can buffer coastal storms
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Researchers moved 306 square meters of intact salt marsh into the Delta Flume, a large wave-testing facility in Delft, Netherlands, and exposed it to waves as high as 2 meters. After 21 hours, the marsh surface had eroded by an average of just 7 millimeters, while its vegetation suffered progressive damage. The study found that plants can reduce wave energy by more than 10%, and by as much as 50% on lower-energy coasts with waves up to 1 meter. Their effect declines as waves grow higher and vegetation is lost. Researchers say marshes could work alongside dikes and seawalls, not replace them. A Spanish coastal-engineering expert questioned how well the Dutch experiment applies to other coastlines, citing wave periods and mobile seabeds among other factors.

items.title: [news.un.org] UN urges steep fossil-fuel cuts as 1.5°C overshoot becomes unavoidable
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

The United Nations Environment Programme’s (UNEP) 2026 Emissions Gap Report says governments must now limit the scale and duration of global warming beyond 1.5°C, rather than try to prevent that threshold from being crossed. Its lowest-overshoot pathway would cap warming at 1.7°C to 1.8°C around mid-century, with about a 50% chance of returning to 1.5°C by 2100. Following that pathway requires greenhouse-gas emissions to fall 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040, compared with 2025. The report says existing national climate pledges would cut emissions by only 5% to 8% by 2030 and 11% to 15% by 2035. If current policies continue, warming could reach 2.8°C this century; full delivery of pledges would still leave it at about 2.6°C. The pathway also calls for sharply reducing coal-fired electricity generation and scaling up carbon removal. The report warns that the required reductions are far beyond current plans. Governments are due to discuss climate action at the COP31 summit, scheduled to open in Antalya on Nov. 9.

items.title: [reuters.com] Putin agrees in principle to resume Ukraine peace talks after Nov. 10 as Kyiv urges ceasefire
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed in principle to resume U.S.-mediated talks with Ukraine after Nov. 10, following a nearly three-hour meeting on Oct. 21 with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg. Kremlin foreign-policy adviser Yuri Ushakov said the technical-level negotiations could take place in Abu Dhabi and focus on a postwar security framework for Russia and Ukraine. Earlier rounds yielded little progress beyond prisoner exchanges. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv supports resuming the talks as soon as possible, preferably by early November, and proposed freezing the current front line as a first step toward a ceasefire. He also called for Ukraine to be included in decisions about its future and said Ukraine’s parliament must approve any peace settlement. Witkoff brought Putin proposals discussed a day earlier with Zelenskyy and European officials in Oslo, including security guarantees and postwar arrangements. Ushakov said the proposals contained little useful material. Moscow continues to seek terms Kyiv rejects, including Russian control of all of Donetsk and a bar on Ukrainian NATO membership. A technical-level meeting is the next step, but no firm date or venue has been announced. The Kremlin said talks could begin after Nov. 10.

items.title: [scitechdaily.com] Stanford team revives bleached corals through brief clone contact
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Stanford researchers report that bleached coral fragments fully recovered within seven weeks in laboratory tests after brief contact with healthy, genetically identical clones, according to a study published Oct. 14 in *Science Advances*. Contact lasting five days to a week was sometimes enough; bleached fragments kept a few millimeters away from healthy partners died. Microscopic channels in the corals’ tissues aligned, allowing beneficial algae to move between fragments within three days. Inside bleached fragments, algae populations doubled every four days during the second week. The method requires matching clones, limiting its use across reefs. The researchers plan to test other ways to deliver algae, including collecting it from healthy corals before heat waves.

items.title: [thehackernews.com] Attackers compromise AI gateway LiteLLM 1.107.0 to steal credentials
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Attackers released a malicious version of LiteLLM, an open-source gateway for connecting to AI models, distributing version 1.107.0 through the Python Package Index (PyPI) and Docker images on Oct. 21. The package installed a credential stealer and a backdoor that could collect cloud and AI service keys, private keys, browser data and other secrets. The code could run whenever Python started, even in programs that did not use LiteLLM. LiteLLM said attackers used three engineers’ GitHub credentials to alter and approve the release, but it has not identified how they obtained those credentials. PyPI removed the package, and affected Docker image tags were removed or replaced. The company advised users to rebuild from a clean environment, rotate exposed credentials and use version 1.106.2 while the investigation continues.

items.title: [koaa.com] U.S. emissions rise worsens global warming outlook, UN report says
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

The United Nations Environment Programme’s (UNEP) 2026 emissions assessment says U.S. greenhouse-gas emissions rose by 133 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2025, the largest increase among major economies. The United States accounted for about 70% of the net increase among 124 countries whose emissions grew. The report warns that the world can no longer avoid exceeding the Paris Agreement’s 1.5°C threshold and must limit the overshoot. The U.S. increase reflected higher electricity demand and a rebound in coal-fired power generation, while global greenhouse-gas emissions remained roughly level at 58.4 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent. The assessment attributes its worsening projections partly to the United States’ formal withdrawal from the Paris Agreement and revised estimates of historical emissions. Under existing policies, warming could reach 2.8°C this century; fully meeting national climate pledges would still leave it at about 2.6°C. UNEP says a pathway offering about a 50% chance of limiting peak warming to 1.7–1.8°C and returning to 1.5°C by 2100 requires global emissions cuts of 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040, relative to 2025. The next UN climate summit, COP31, is scheduled to open in Antalya, Türkiye, next month.

Google-owned security company Wiz independently used Google’s Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI models to identify vulnerabilities in the same core software. PHP maintainers released fixes on Oct. 21 for the two flaws, which had remained hidden for years and could let attackers run code on vulnerable servers without authentication (fortune.com, wiz.io, reuters.com). Wiz said frontier models made a complex exploit chain substantially easier to execute, describing steps that had once been at the edge of what human researchers could achieve (wiz.io). The same capabilities could help attackers adapt exploits to different PHP versions and server configurations, the company warned (techcrunch.com, axios.com). OpenAI said it believes researchers found the flaws before attackers did. It is proposing a repeatable process for identifying and fixing vulnerabilities in widely used software and preparing defenses against them. The company said it expects similar discoveries to increase sharply in coming months (openai.com). Vulnerability surge: A graph compiled by research nonprofit Epoch AI showed significant vulnerabilities reported by major technology companies and open-source projects rising from a few dozen in some months several years ago to about 600 in a typical month (motherjones.com). OpenAI funding: OpenAI pledged $1 billion in subsidized Daybreak access for frontline defenders, with a focus on organizations that have limited security resources (openai.com). Exposure checker: OpenAI published a PHP version-checking tool as a Codex skill to help operators identify potentially vulnerable installations and determine relevant updates (openai.com). Proof-of-concept video: An accidentally posted video showed an exploit working against multiple targets; copies spread online and contributed to faster development and circulation of exploit demonstrations (simonwillison.net).
